correctness.rationale: For the positive rational maps, put Z=(a+Y)/X and W=(b+Z)/Y. The three numerator factors of R_(b,a)(Z,W) become (aX+bY+ab)/X, Z(bX+a)/Y and W(aY+b), respectively. Cancellation proves the integral identity before taking the locally uniform logarithmic limit, so H is conserved including switching lines. Expanding the maxima gives the seven nonconstant half-plane bounds and the constant 3. Their consecutive intersections give the seven displayed vertices for h>3; the seven edge directions and positive primitive lengths give perimeter 5h-8, and the shoelace sum gives twice the stated area. Each branch of F is orientation-preserving unimodular and preserves primitive tangent vectors up to transformation to another primitive vector. Subdivision at switches suffices for positive arclength preservation; the inverse and conservation make this a circle isometry. The image of P_0 is P_3, distance 3h-5 counterclockwise; the resulting fractional-linear ratio has derivative 1/(5h-8)^2 and is rational exactly for rational h. Dividing this derivative by the area action derivative proves the twist. On integer exterior shells the primitive coordinate runs through exactly the full set of residues modulo 5k-8; the shift is coprime by the stated Bézout identity. At h=3 the half-planes imply that the integer rows are y=0 with x=-1,0,1 and y=1 with x=-1,0,1,2. Direct substitution verifies the seven-cycle. No real-circle claim is made for that central level.

value.rationale: The alternating map canonically changes the simplest max-Lyness setting. Its explicit translation is an all-shell classification, with a nontrivial distinction between rational and irrational real levels and, more strongly, transitivity and exact periods throughout the lattice. The perimeter–shift coprimality and central seven-cycle quantify what a generic rotation theorem or finite orbit plotting cannot answer.
residual_risks: Only this schedule and stroboscopic map are classified, and the continuous dynamics of the flat central level is outside scope.
